patients.summary: Marketing consultant and mother of four with GAD, stress urinary incontinence after her fourth delivery and uterine fibroids. At 45 she has a sixth pregnancy with fetal trisomy 21 confirmed by amniocentesis and late oligohydramnios, delivered vaginally at 36w5d; now postpartum with anxiety followed in primary care.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT / PREVENTIVE

40F, marketing consultant (works mostly from home, some client travel), transferring care. Wanted an office where she can actually reach her doctor. Delivered her 4th baby this past June, feels like she is getting her body back.

PMH
- Generalized anxiety disorder: dx at her old PCP years ago. Never took medication, does fine most of the time with exercise and keeping a tight schedule. Worry ramps up around deadlines and when the kids are sick.
- Gallstones seen on an ultrasound at some point before now. No attacks since, never had surgery, nobody recommended it.

OB: G5P4014. Four term vaginal deliveries, first at 39 wk; the last one (June 2020) had a long pushing stage. One early miscarriage with a D&C. No other surgery.

Meds: prenatal vitamin daily (kept taking it after delivery).
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: mother had fibroids. No chromosomal or genetic conditions in the family that she knows of.
SH: married, four children at home. Never smoked. Doesn't drink.

ROS: tired in the way you are with an infant. Otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Well appearing, pleasant. Eyes, ears, throat unremarkable. Neck supple, thyroid normal size. Heart regular rate, no murmurs. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, no RUQ tenderness. Legs without swelling. Skin clear. Mood good, affect bright, a little rushed.

GAD-7 7, PHQ-9 3.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH, A1c today. One-time HIV and hep C screening, she agrees. Flu shot given. Will order a screening mammogram for after the new year. Pap 2019 per her, normal; will confirm with old records.
2. GAD, mild by today's score. No interest in meds. Return if it gets harder to manage.
3. Gallstones, asymptomatic. Nothing to do unless symptoms.
4. Records release signed for the prior office.

Annual visit next fall.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM to left deltoid. Patient tolerated well, no reaction. VIS provided.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Aisha, all of your labs from Wednesday look good. Blood counts, kidney and liver function, sugar and thyroid are normal, cholesterol is in a healthy range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Nothing to change. Talk soon.

documents.title: Prior primary care records received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Records from her previous primary care office reviewed (42 pages).

Relevant:
- Cervical cytology 2019: negative for intraepithelial lesion. Next due 2024 with co-testing.
- Tdap given in 2020 during her last pregnancy.
- Generalized anxiety disorder on the problem list, no medications ever prescribed.
- Gallstones noted on a prior abdominal ultrasound, no follow-up imaging, no surgery.
- Allergies: NKDA.

No other active problems. Immunization record updated. Scanned to media.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views with tomosynthesis. No prior studies available for comparison. The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications. Skin and nipples unremarkable.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your mammogram is normal. Dense breast tissue was noted, which is common and just means we keep screening on schedule. See you in the fall.

documents.title: Covid vaccine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Fully vaccinated as of last week. Pfizer, first shot April 7 and the second on April 28 at the regional mass vaccination site. Card photo attached. Second one knocked me out for a day.

documents.title: RE: Covid vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Aisha, both doses are entered in your record now.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam.

Doing well. Baby is 16 months and sleeping through the night most nights, which has helped everything. Back to a full client load. Walking most mornings.

Anxiety: steady. GAD-7 6. Uses running lists and the walks; doesn't want medication.
No GI symptoms, no RUQ pain.
Meds: prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: BP and weight per flowsheet, down about a kilo from last year. Throat and ears clear. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin unremarkable.

Plan
- CBC, CMP, lipids.
- Flu vaccine today.
- Mammogram ordered for early next year.
- Pap not due until 2024.
- Covid: primary series done in April; booster when she becomes eligible.

RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Aisha, labs from the physical are all normal again this year. Have a good fall.

documents.title: COVID-19 Booster
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pfizer booster 0.3 mL IM to the right arm. Screening questions all no. Waited 15 minutes in the office, no reaction. CDC card updated.

documents.title: Booster question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Do I need another covid booster yet? A friend said there's a new one.

documents.title: RE: Booster question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Aisha, you had your booster in November, so you're up to date for now. We'll let you know when anything new is recommended for your age group.

reports.text: Bilateral digital mammography with tomosynthesis, compared with 2021. Heterogeneously dense breast tissue. No new or suspicious mass, distortion or calcification. Stable appearance.

orders.reason: Urinary leakage with exertion since last delivery

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Came in specifically for this, a little embarrassed to bring it up. Since the baby two years ago she leaks urine when she jumps with the kids on the trampoline, sneezes, or laughs hard. Wears a pad every day now. It has started to keep her from things, she has started turning down client dinners because she doesn't want to be caught out. No pain with urination, no blood. Doesn't get up at night to void.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Abdomen soft, nontender, no suprapubic tenderness. Pelvic exam deferred to gyn.
UA dip and micro: negative.

A/P: Exertional urine leakage after vaginal deliveries, sounds like stress type. UA clean. She'd like to see gynecology for a proper pelvic floor evaluation. Referral placed. In the meantime gave her a handout on pelvic floor squeezes.

documents.title: Gyn referral
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Aisha, your gynecology referral was sent. Their scheduling office will contact you, and their first opening is early July. Let us know if you don't hear from them within a week.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology group
Date of visit: 07/06/2022
Re: Aisha Pierre, DOB 11/21/1979

Thank you for referring Ms. Pierre, a 42-year-old G5P4014, for urinary leakage.

She describes leaking with sneezing, laughing and physical activity, starting after her most recent vaginal delivery about two years ago, a delivery notable for a prolonged second stage. She uses a pad every day and finds the accidents unpredictable enough to make social plans stressful. She has no nocturia, urgency or dysuria.

PMH: generalized anxiety disorder. OB: four term SVDs, one first-trimester loss with D&C.
Medications: prenatal vitamin daily. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with uterine fibroids. No familial chromosomal or genetic disorders.
Social: marketing consultant; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: external genitalia normal. On speculum and bimanual exam, mild uterine descent with Valsalva and slight laxity of the anterior vaginal wall. Post-void residual by bladder scan 25 mL.

A three-day voiding diary she completed before the visit shows normal daytime frequency, with small-volume leakage episodes linked to laughing and jumping.

Impression: stress urinary incontinence.

Plan: We reviewed conservative first-line management. I taught pelvic floor muscle (Kegel) contractions and explained that strengthening the voluntary muscles around the urethra and bladder neck improves closure under pressure. Also discussed timed voiding before exercise and limiting caffeine. We will hold off on pessary, medication or surgical options while she gives the exercises a fair trial. Follow up in about three months.

Allergies: NKDA.

Sincerely,
Gynecology

documents.title: Gyn visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Aisha, the gynecology note came through. They agree it's stress incontinence and started you on pelvic floor exercises with a recheck in about three months. Hang in there with the exercises, they take a while to pay off.

documents.title: Gynecology Follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology group
Date of visit: 10/03/2022
Re: Aisha Pierre

Ms. Pierre returns for the stress incontinence we evaluated in July. Despite doing the exercises, leakage with coughing and sneezing has been getting steadily worse over the last few months, and she has also noticed going more often during the day with some urgency. No dysuria, no hematuria.

New today: she reports a year of heavy periods and a sense of pelvic pressure.

Medications: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA. Family history of fibroids in her mother.

Exam: abdomen soft and nontender. Bimanual exam: the uterus is enlarged with an irregular contour and is not tender. No adnexal masses, no adnexal tenderness.

Urinalysis in clinic normal.

Assessment:
1. Uterine leiomyoma, clinically; likely contributing to the pressure symptoms.
2. Stress urinary incontinence, progressing despite pelvic floor training.

Plan:
- Pelvic ultrasound to characterize the uterus.
- Referral to urogynecology for further evaluation of the incontinence.
- Continue pelvic floor exercises in the meantime.

Allergies: NKDA.

Gynecology

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal imaging. The uterus is anteverted and enlarged, measuring 11.2 x 6.8 x 7.4 cm, with a lobular contour. Three intramural fibroids: 3.9 cm posterior fundal, 2.6 cm anterior body, and 1.8 cm left lateral. Endometrium measures 7 mm and is not distorted. Both ovaries are normal in size and appearance. No adnexal mass. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged fibroid uterus with three intramural leiomyomas, largest 3.9 cm. Normal ovaries.

documents.title: Ultrasound
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your pelvic ultrasound shows fibroids, three of them, the largest just under 4 cm. Your ovaries look normal. This fits with the heavy periods and the pressure. Gynecology will go over options with you; we can also talk about it at your physical next week.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual.

Interval: saw gyn in July and again two weeks ago for the leakage. Dx stress incontinence; doing Kegels, honestly not much better, and gyn is sending her on to urogyn. At the October visit gyn also found an enlarged uterus, and the pelvic US last week showed three intramural fibroids, biggest 3.9 cm. Mom had the same. Periods are heavy for 2 days, pressure low in the pelvis. No lightheadedness.

Anxiety a little higher this fall with a big client launch, GAD-7 8. Still not interested in medication, would rather ride it out.

Meds: prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, weight down slightly. Throat clear, no thyromegaly. RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender; I can't feel the uterus abdominally. No edema.

A/P
- Fibroids with heavy menses: CBC today to look for anemia. Following with gyn.
- SUI: urogyn referral in process via gyn.
- GAD: mild-moderate, monitor.
- CMP, lipids. Flu and bivalent covid booster today. Mammogram order for spring.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Aisha, your hemoglobin is 12.3, which is normal, so the heavier periods have not made you anemic. The rest of the labs are normal too. If the bleeding gets heavier or you start feeling washed out, let me know and we'll recheck.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good to know, thank you!
